sections.h2: Who values, bills and collects Letcher County property tax
sections.html:
Letcher County runs its tax through a valuation office, the sheriff and the clerk. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets each parcel's value. The Letcher County Sheriff sends out the bill and receives the payment. The Letcher County Clerk inherits anything still unpaid in mid-April.

The PVA sits at 156 Main Street, Suite 105, in Whitesburg, with a phone line at 606-633-2182 and a fax at 606-633-3995. Ownership, like value, is fixed on January 1, so a house bought in March still shows the seller on that year's bill. A new owner who never sees a copy can phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293.

The sheriff keeps weekday hours of 8:30 to 4 and offers a web page for paying the bill. The clerk, at 606-633-2432, keeps the same hours and runs a delinquent tax section. Phone the clerk to learn when the current year's tax sale is scheduled.

sections.h2: Letcher County housing at a glance
sections.html:
Letcher is a mountain county where the land shapes how a house is priced and how long it sits. Whitesburg is the seat, Jenkins is the biggest city, and Fleming-Neon makes three. The county had an estimated 19,952 residents in July 2025, down 7.4 percent from 21,548 in 2020. It has 8,463 households, and 74.1 percent of homes are owner occupied. The middle home value is $67,400 and median rent is $669.

With almost no new construction, nearly every sale is a resale, and buyers compare each house against a small set of older homes. A tax bill on a low-value home is small in dollars, which is why a few years of neglect can feel manageable until the penalties compound. Flooding in July and August 2022 damaged homes in the county, so if a building was hit, ask the PVA how that damage shows up in the assessment.

Kentucky's collection statute, KRS 134.015, sets one calendar for every county, and the sheriff here follows it.

Letcher County tax bill by payment date
Date paidWhat you owe
Through November 1Bill minus 2 percent
Early November to December 31Face amount
JanuaryFace amount plus 5 percent
February onwardFace amount plus 10 percent and the sheriff's fee

If the state delays a county's bills, it can swap in a schedule that allows a month per stage.

sections.h2: If the bill is still unpaid after April 15
sections.html:
Closing time on April 15 is the cliff. The sheriff hands the open bills to the clerk. Each one is reissued as a certificate of delinquency, and the lien attaches to your house. Monthly interest of one percent starts, and the clerk and county attorney each earn commissions that climb as notices go out.

The Revenue Department's sample shows the pace of growth. A $1,000 bill reaches the clerk at $1,254 once the penalty, fee and commission are added. If it is still open after the June newspaper ad, the sample total is $1,659.90. A public sale follows three to four and a half months after the handoff, where investors may buy the debt. The lien can last eleven years whoever owns the house.

Begin with a sit-down at the PVA's office. The appeals panel refuses any case that skipped that meeting, and the meeting must happen before or during the viewing window.

The roll opens for public viewing on May's first Monday and stays open thirteen days. Once you have held your conference, you must file with the Letcher County Clerk by the end of the workday that follows the window. The local appeals panel then sits in Whitesburg, the county seat, roughly a month later, within 25 to 35 days of the window closing.

  • Evidence to bring: lot and building details, insurance policies, construction costs and listings of comparable houses. An appeal with no evidence is denied.
  • A paid advocate has to be a lawyer, accountant, consultant, broker, appraiser, your own employee or a holder of a state-recognized designation, and needs your authorization in writing.
  • Audio recording is allowed, and the panel must explain any change in writing.
  • If bills were printed before the ruling and the value rises, a supplemental bill follows.

sections.h2: Homestead exemption for seniors and disabled owners
sections.html:
The deduction for assessment years 2025 and 2026 is $49,100 of taxable value. The home must be the applicant's residence, and the applicant must either reach 65 during the tax year or hold a total disability rating from a federal program or a retirement system. Roughly one resident in five is past 65, so many owners may qualify.

Apply at the Letcher County PVA. Owners under 65 who claim disability usually renew yearly. The exceptions, who document the disability a single time, are owners with a service-connected disability and owners ruled permanently disabled by Social Security or the state retirement system. A buyer cannot inherit the break, since the exemption belongs to the person.

sections.h2: What a Letcher County seller owes at closing
sections.html:
The bill follows the January 1 titleholder, and the settlement statement decides who reimburses whom. A common Kentucky practice is for the seller to credit the buyer for the months of ownership, with the buyer paying the full bill when it arrives.

The state's deed transfer tax (KRS 142.050) falls on the seller. The charge is fifty cents per $500 of the price on the deed, and a partial block counts as a whole one. The clerk takes it at the recording window. Foreclosure transfers, spouses splitting in a divorce and nominal parent-child transfers are exempt. Because delinquent tax is a lien, closing agents insist on paying it out of the proceeds. Before closing, line up the sheriff's payoff figure and the clerk's answer on any delinquency certificate.

sections.h2: Selling a house with back taxes
sections.html:
Start with two phone calls. Dial the sheriff at 606-633-2293 for this year's amount plus any older year left open. Then dial the clerk at 606-633-2432 to learn if a certificate already exists on the parcel. Request each figure in writing and note the date it stays good, because interest runs monthly.

Pass both figures to the title company ahead of signing any contract. Whatever is owed comes out of your sale money at closing, so no cash needs to change hands beforehand. A cash buyer can still close on a house carrying a lien once the payoff is pinned down, and the lien is cleared at the table.

faqs.q: Who gets the Letcher County tax payment?
faqs.a: Send it to the Letcher County Sheriff, who answers at 606-633-2293 on weekdays from 8:30 to 4. The county website also links to an online payment page. Anything unpaid after April 15 shifts to the county clerk.

faqs.q: Is there an early-payment discount in Letcher County?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the whole bill by November 1 of the tax year takes 2 percent off. From then through year end you pay the printed figure, and two penalty steps come next: 5 percent, then 10.

faqs.q: I bought in Letcher County and no bill came. What now?
faqs.a: Phone the sheriff at 606-633-2293 and ask for a copy. Bills are written to the owner on January 1, so yours may be under the seller's name. Not receiving the bill does not cancel what is owed.

faqs.q: Who hears a property tax appeal in Letcher County?
faqs.a: The local board of assessment appeals, meeting in Whitesburg. You first meet the PVA at 156 Main Street, Suite 105, then file with the clerk. The filing deadline is the workday after the thirteen-day roll inspection ends.

faqs.q: Who pays the year's tax when a Letcher County house changes hands?
faqs.a: The settlement statement decides. The sheriff bills the January 1 owner, and sellers commonly credit the buyer for their months of ownership. Delinquent amounts are a lien that has to be cleared for the title to pass clean.
